claims.text: The low-dimensional state governs the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type films or nanoribbons.
Heat-transfer rate governs the magnetocaloric response and hysteresis.
Non-equiatomic composition affects magnetic ordering and domain-wall dynamics.
Magnetic domain walls and spin configurations mediate the response to low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Magnetoelastic coupling and spin-lattice interactions are the operative mechanism.
The low-dimensional material will show a 20% reduction in magnetocaloric response relative to the stated as-deposited bulk baseline.
The low-dimensional material will show a 30% increase in hysteresis relative to the stated as-deposited bulk baseline.
Heat-transfer rate limits magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
The proposed mechanism and predictions apply from 250 to 350 K.
The proposed mechanism and predictions apply over magnetic fields from 0 to 1 T.
The exact magnetic ordering and domain-wall dynamics in the low-dimensional state are not well understood.
In-situ TEM or X-ray spectroscopy combined with atomistic simulations can test the proposed mechanism while magnetocaloric response and hysteresis are measured.
A measured magnetocaloric response within 10% of the predicted value would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state is a nanoscale film or nanoribbon, but the named baseline is an as-deposited bulk form. Thus, the phrase 'relative to the as-deposited baseline' conflates deposition state with dimensional form and does not provide a matched low-dimensional control.
Agreement within 10% of the predicted magnetocaloric response would ordinarily support the quantitative prediction, not falsify it. The stated falsification rule is logically inverted.
